originality.rationale: Voits–Schwarz arXiv:2611.06490v1 proves sufficient affine local perturbation for occupation mutual linearity, not a full-vector converse, projective inverse, all-dimension preservation or exact reset-scan identifiability boundary. Voits arXiv:2610.13505v1 and Bradley et al. (2003) give forward semi-Markov transforms/aggregation. The closest published published-finding corpus identifiability hit observes trap-position distributions, and the closest semi-Markov response hit handles a fixed three-state model; neither implies this complete local joint-kernel inverse. Classical resolvent mathematics supplies the starting point, and implicit prior inverse-equivalence remains a risk.
residual_risks: A classical renewal-resolvent or Schur-complement theorem could have previously formulated an equivalent inverse under background-known assumptions; not all historic inverse-semi-Markov sources are indexed.
The physical inference value assumes ideal complete all-rate stationarity or all-time transient measurements; noisy finite-rate recovery is impossible without additional modeling restrictions.
The prior sufficient affine theorem is explicitly credited; the novelty is only the complete converse/inverse, arbitrary-dimension rigidity, and identifiability boundary.

value.rationale: A natural information-completeness question for finite statistical-mechanics networks with memory is resolved: one age-zero start and complete state occupations uniquely recover all unknown destination-dependent exit-time measures, and an all-rate resetting experiment yields the same information without observing jumps. The full-vector affine-response criterion becomes necessary as well as sufficient, and all affine ranks are preserved. The sharp finite-rate nonidentifiability result places a concrete experimental boundary on that recovery. This is a motivated complete classification of what observations determine, not a routine parameter substitution, and no stability or downstream experimental theorem is asserted.
